extracted.intended_audience: scholars, editors, and readers of historical literary texts (editors preparing a scholarly edition of The Spectator)
extracted.subtask_short: editing a scholarly edition of The Spectator
extracted.subtask_description: Editorial guidelines for producing a scholarly reprint of The Spectator: reproduce original authorial text and typographic features, document revisions, and provide supporting notes and appendices (translations, advertisements, index) for reader reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reprint text as authors left it
rubrics_metrics.description: This volume reprints for the first time in the present century the text of the 'Spectator' as its authors left it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give the original text precisely as left after revision by the authors; avoid wilful alteration of the text. Compare daily issues, revised octavo issues, and last edition before Steele's death to show the amount and character of revision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restore original punctuation and emphasis practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Restore to their style the proper harmony of the authors' own methods of punctuating, and their way of sometimes getting emphasis by the use of capitals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not modernize punctuation arbitrarily; modernization has been counted a defect in instances where it changes sense. Preserve original punctuation and capitalization that function as emphasis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retain original spelling when sense is clear
rubrics_metrics.description: As the few differences between good spelling in Queen Anne's time and good spelling now are never of a kind to obscure the sense, it has been thought better to make the reproduction perfect, and thus show not only what Steele and Addison wrote, but how they spelt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer faithful reproduction of historical spelling rather than modernizing, unless a variant materially obscures meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mark sentences added in the reprint with square brackets
rubrics_metrics.description: Sentences added in the reprint are placed between square brackets [ ], without any appended note.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use square brackets to indicate text that did not appear in the original issues but has been inserted in this edition; do not append separate explanatory notes for such insertions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show omissions/alterations by bracketing and footnote
rubrics_metrics.description: Sentences omitted, or words altered, are shown by bracketing the revised version, and giving the text as it stood in the original daily issue within corresponding brackets as a foot-note.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When material present in one witness (e.g., daily issue) is omitted or altered in the revised text, indicate the revised form in brackets in the main text and provide the original daily-issue reading in a correspondingly-bracketed footnote to preserve both readings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow original folio numbering and typographic details
rubrics_metrics.description: The original folio numbers have been followed also in the use of _italics_ [_shown between underscored thus_] and other little details of the disposition of the type; for example, rows of single inverted commas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserve original pagination references, italics (transcribed by agreed conventions such as underscores), and other typographic features of the original imprint; note any formatting details not reproduced in a particular electronic file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Place translations of mottos and Latin quotations in an Appendix
rubrics_metrics.description: The translation of the mottos and Latin quotations, which Steele and Addison deliberately abstained from giving, and which, as they were since added, impede and sometimes confound and contradict the text, are here placed in a body at the end, for those who want them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep translations separate from the main text to avoid confusing or contradicting the original text; provide them in an appendix for readers who wish to consult them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include original advertisements in an Appendix when illustrative
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a short Appendix also of advertisements taken from the original number of the 'Spectator', and a few others, where they seem to illustrate some point in the text, will be found among the notes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reproduce contemporary advertisements and similar paratextual materials in an appendix when they illuminate the text or historical context; integrate them into notes where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide explanatory notes for historical/contextual understanding
rubrics_metrics.description: In the large number of notes here added to a revision of those bequeathed to us by Percy and Calder, the object has been to give information which may contribute to some nearer acquaintance with the writers of the book, and enjoyment of allusions to past manners and events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add notes that supply biographical, historical, and cultural context, clarify allusions, and, where possible, resolve questions of authorship or reference to aid reader comprehension and enjoyment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and augment existing General Index for reference
rubrics_metrics.description: From the 'General Index to the Spectators, &c.,' published as a separate volume in 1760, there has been taken what was serviceable, and additions have been made to it with a desire to secure for this edition of the 'Spectator' the advantages of being handy for reference as well as true to the real text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate useful material from earlier indexes and augment them as needed so the edition is both accurate to the text and convenient for reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid editorial correction of authors' style and grammar
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors of another 'understanding age' have also taken upon themselves by many a little touch to correct Addison's style or grammar; such modernization has been to the destruction of the freshness of the original style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refrain from 'improving' or correcting an author's grammar or style merely to suit modern taste; preserve original linguistic character to maintain authenticity and freshness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document editorial comparisons and show character of revisions
rubrics_metrics.description: The papers as they first appeared in the daily issue ... have been closely compared with the first issue in guinea octavos ... and with the last edition that appeared before the death of Steele. The original text is here given precisely as it was left after revision by its authors; and there is shown at the same time the amount and character of the revision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct collational comparisons among witnesses (daily numbers, revised octavos, later editions) and make the process and results visible to readers by showing variant readings and noting the nature of revisions.
